title: Analytic number theory, zeta functions and prime distribution, Part II: the effective class number problem
summary: Extend the analytic class-number interfaces to Goldfeld’s effective lower bounds for imaginary quadratic fields. The proof combines positive Mellin kernels, modular elliptic L-functions with a third-order central zero, Gross–Zagier heights, genus theory and certified numerical estimates. Construct explicit discriminant bounds and a complete certified enumeration of the class number three fields, with independent arithmetic and analytic rank certificates for the two elliptic curves.
readme: The definitive reader is research/blueprint/readmes/AnalyticNumberTheoryPartII.md. Six layers extend the parent’s quadratic-character and class-number interfaces to positive Mellin comparison, two independently certified rank-three curves, effective logarithmic lower bounds and the sixteen imaginary quadratic fields of class number three. Generic quadratic arithmetic, modularity, Gross–Zagier theory and validated numerics are imported from their existing owners; the concrete certificate targets and the analytic comparison are developed here.

stages.title: Quadratic class numbers and ramified weights
stages.description: Import the existing ideal class number, fundamental discriminants, genus divisibility, and current IntegralLattices Layer B binary-form/class dictionary and finite reduction enumeration. Define the discriminant weight θ(d) excluding the largest prime. Prove p^h≥d/4 for a split prime and quantify agreement of the quadratic character with Liouville below this threshold. GN.3 supplies the native class-group, discriminant and boundary/counting adapters and integrated nonaxial estimate; AN.4 supplies partial-zeta formulas.

stages.title: Goldfeld’s effective analytic principle
stages.description: Define the degree four completion and the positive inverse Mellin kernel. Prove the positive-measure comparison under integrated cumulative domination, the reflection contour identity, the truncated residue formula and the three remainder estimates. From Oesterlé’s exact C1–C4 hypotheses prove a uniform, effectively computed technical class-number bound whose constant depends only on Ψ and M, not on K or G.

stages.title: Two certified rank three curves
stages.description: Construct the native models of E₁₃₉ and E₅₀₇₇ and their source-model comparisons. Import modularity, actual entire elliptic L-functions, quadratic twists, Heegner heights and descent algorithms. Certify conductor 37·139² and 5077, root number −1, arithmetic rank 3, exact vanishing of the first derivative and nonvanishing of the third derivative. Develop the BGZ kernels and rigorous derivative enclosures, including the height gap that upgrades a numerical enclosure to exact zero.

stages.title: Uniform logarithmic class-number bounds
stages.description: Build Ψ,G,M satisfying C1–C4 from the two rank-three newforms. Include every overlap between discriminant and elliptic conductor, all ramified Euler corrections and the finitely many scales M. Certify θ(d)log d≤7000h for every negative fundamental discriminant; certify θ(d)log d≤55h when (d,5077)=1. Prove the fallback split-prime estimate and the fundamental-discriminant congruence exclusion of |discr K|=5077 used in class number three.

stages.title: Explicit constants and effective finiteness
stages.description: Define the explicit prime-product majorants C_7000 and C_55 and prove C(t)h≥log d on their stated families. Prove log C_c(t)∼4√(t/log t) by importing PNT from AN.2. Construct a rational algorithm κ(q)>0 and prove the strict lower bound κ(ε)(log d)^(1−ε)<h for every ε>0. Supply an explicit finite cutoff for every prescribed class number, keeping this effective logarithmic bound separate from Siegel’s stronger ineffective power bound.

stages.title: The class number three discriminants
stages.description: Certify the Montgomery–Weinberger exclusion for 10^12≤d≤10^2500 from the three auxiliary primitive real odd characters χ_{−17923},χ_{−115147},χ_{−123204}, phase inequalities and critical-line-zero brackets. Certify the Lehmer–Lehmer–Shanks small-range sieve above 907, regenerating finite character-pattern certificates. Combine the logarithmic cutoff, the prime-discriminant consequence of genus theory and exact reduced-form enumeration to obtain precisely the sixteen discriminants −23,−31,−59,−83,−107,−139,−211,−283,−307,−331,−379,−499,−547,−643,−883,−907, and largest absolute value 907.
